lesson_title: Say It Before You Build It
hook_text: Before a single piece of card is cut, the crane exists on one page: what it must do, and what you are not allowed to use.
clip_script: A scrap dealer needs steel pulled out of a mixed pile. That is a need. Turn it into a brief: design a model crane with an electromagnet that lifts steel, swings it to a bin and lets go. What, who for, what it must do. Now the specifications: things you can test. Lift ten clips. Drop them within one second. Move them 200 millimetres. Pick up no copper. Then the constraints: the limits on you. Card, string, a nail, two cells, an A4 base, four periods, no mains. Ask one question of every line: is this about the crane, or about me? Crane means specification. Me means constraint. Two columns, one page, and now you know exactly what winning looks like.
visual_style: Whiteboard sentence building word by word; two columns filling with short lines; a tick appearing beside each testable line.
mood: Brisk and clarifying, a coach drawing the plan.
pacing: Need, brief, specs, constraints, the one question, each a few seconds.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and write the brief for your own crane.
